messages.author: 59ddd620b9f8604d
messages.subject: scantwo
parts:
I was trying to interpret the plot.scantwo, but here is what confused
me:
As far as I understand, we have 3 models, NULL, full and additive
models. Joint LOD score compares the full model with null model;
Epistasis LOD score compares the full model with additive model;
Additive LOD score compare the additive model with NULL model. We can
also compare the additive model with single QTL model to get the
conditional Addive LOD score or compare the full model with single QTL
model to get the conditional interative model. Is that right? If I am
correct, then the help file of plot.scantwo is has some errors because
the epstasis LOD score is explained in a different way. I am using the
latest version 1.01-9

Another question is about missing genotypes. I know the individuals
with missing genotypes are dropped for scanone, but If 20-30% of
genotypes is missing for certain marker, will it affect the estimation
of the LOD score?

Last question. For a backcross case, if for certain marker, the ratio
of A/H is not 1:1, instead it is about 1:2 or 2:1, and the p-val is
0.005, what I can say about it? ( assume there is few or no missing
genotypes) and what precaution should I take when I do scanone or
scantwo? Or it does not matter?

Can anyone help me out on this? Thanks

messages.author: f388084a0de67b60
messages.subject: Re: scantwo
parts:
>
> I was trying to interpret the plot.scantwo, but here is what confused
> me:
> As far as I understand, we have 3 models, NULL, full and additive
> models. Joint LOD score compares the full model with null model;
> Epistasis LOD score compares the full model with additive model;
> Additive LOD score compare the additive model with NULL model. We can
> also compare the additive model with single QTL model to get the
> conditional Addive LOD score or compare the full model with single QTL
> model to get the conditional interative model. Is that right? If I am
> correct, then the help file of plot.scantwo is has some errors because
> the epstasis LOD score is explained in a different way. I am using the
> latest version 1.01-9

Indeed, there's a typo: the epistasis LOD score is the log10 likelihood
for the full model minus the log10 likelihood for the additive model.

> Another question is about missing genotypes. I know the individuals
> with missing genotypes are dropped for scanone, but If 20-30% of
> genotypes is missing for certain marker, will it affect the estimation
> of the LOD score?

In both scanone() and scantwo(), individuals with missing genotype
data are *not* dropped (except if you use method="mr", which we
recommend
against). Individuals with missing phenotype data are dropped.

> Last question. For a backcross case, if for certain marker, the ratio
> of A/H is not 1:1, instead it is about 1:2 or 2:1, and the p-val is
> 0.005, what I can say about it? ( assume there is few or no missing
> genotypes) and what precaution should I take when I do scanone or
> scantwo? Or it does not matter?

Such segregation distortion might indicate errors in the genotype data.
If it's real segregation distortion, it has some influence on our
efforts to reconstruct the missing genotype data, and so the
calculations
we are doing are less than idea. But for the most part, the results of
scanone() and scantwo() should be little influenced by segregation
distortion, as the analyses are conditional on the observed genotypes.
If one had quite complete genotype data and relatively dense markers,
segregation distortion will not affect things at all (except in terms
of the power to detect QTLs: equal allele frequencies results in
greater power).

regards,
karl

messages.author: f388084a0de67b60
messages.subject: Re: scantwo
parts:
It permutes the phenotypes relative to the genotypes (just like in
scanone
permutations) and keeps track of the maximum joint LOD and the maximum
interaction LOD.

karl
